title: Count Vowels with a Set
hints: Lowercase the text and count the characters contained in a set of vowels. Annotate the set's element type so the literal becomes `Set<Character>`.
jsBridge: In JS, `new Set('aeiou')` then `.has(c)`. Swift's `Set<Character>` is the same, and `"aeiou".contains(c)` also works since `String` is a collection. A set literal (`let vowels: Set<Character> = ["a", …]`) makes the O(1) intent explicit.

compass.q: For 5 vowels, is a `Set` really faster than a `String.contains` scan? When does the set win?
JS `Set` keeps insertion order. Does Swift's `Set`? What does that mean for printing or tests?
Is "É" a vowel here? How would you make the check diacritic-insensitive?
Filtering characters shows up in input validation, like allowed characters in a username. Where would you use `CharacterSet` instead?
